idiom: hit the nail on the head
meaning: to describe or identify exactly the right thing or the real cause of a problem
example: Your comment about the late deliveries hit the nail on the head; the schedule was the real problem.
origin: Comes from carpentry, where a hammer strikes the head of a nail squarely so that it goes in straight

wrong_meanings.meaning: to hammer something badly and damage it
wrong_meanings.why_wrong: This describes a physical action done poorly, but the idiom is about accuracy in speech or thinking, not damage.

wrong_meanings.meaning: to spend too much time on small details
wrong_meanings.why_wrong: This describes overthinking, which is the opposite of getting straight to the main point.

wrong_meanings.meaning: to give up on a project before it is finished
wrong_meanings.why_wrong: The idiom is positive and about being correct, so it has nothing to do with stopping work.

explanation: 'Hit the nail on the head' comes from carpentry, where a precise strike drives a nail in cleanly. It means to say or identify exactly what is right or what the real cause is.
